title: Fox’s Stunning Confession – Soberanía 130
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 130 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
return from a week off with a packed show. First, they discuss Vicente Fox
finally saying the quiet part out loud: in an interview the former president
confessed that he "made Calderón win" in 2006, admitted it wasn't very
democratic, and said he wouldn't have handed over power had AMLO been
recognized as the winner.

Next, they analyze the U.S. midterms from a Global South perspective: a
tsunami that flipped both chambers, with Texas electing Democrat James
Talarico and Gina Hinojosa as governor — the first since Ann Richards. The
hosts caution against cheering the Democrats too loudly, noting their
complicity in the Cuba blockade, the El Mayo kidnapping, and the Iran war, but
argue the rebuke of Trump — a monster who deserves The Hague — creates space
for maneuver.

Then, they celebrate Lula's fourth-term victory in Brazil: a four-million-vote
margin, nearly three million more voters turning out in the second round, and
a campaign that combined a 10-million-subscriber WhatsApp channel with
decentralized, street-level organizing. They also note Flávio's brief, absurd
self-declaration as president-elect from Miami before the State Department
made him walk it back.

Losers and Haters takes aim at the Associated Press for a badly sourced piece
on the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo, which buries the
allegations against his widow and successor until three-quarters of the way in
— and launders Miguel Mesa, a political operative tied to the opposition who
admits receiving intelligence from U.S. security agencies, as a "researcher."
The hosts call it lazy, complicit journalism that feeds the U.S. agenda in the
region.
